claims.text: Raw sensor data from ubiquitous devices can be translated into markers of mental health-related behaviors and states using a layered, hierarchical model.

evidence.description: The authors propose a layered, hierarchical model designed specifically for translating raw sensor data into markers of behaviors and states related to mental health.

methodologies.name: Layered hierarchical translation model
methodologies.description: A framework for converting raw data stream traces from smartphones, wearables, social media, and computers into behavioral and psychological markers.

limitations.text: Personal sensing research is constrained by privacy concerns surrounding daily life data collection.
Personal sensing methodologies face data high-dimensionality challenges.

future_work.text: Application of personal sensing as a clinical tool for monitoring at-risk populations.
Development of next-generation mobile health (mHealth) interventions built on personal sensing foundations.
